title.narrative: Lifesaving assistance for newly affected people in hard-to-reach and underserved areas the northeast ( KACHIN )

description.narrative: ltpgtIn accordance with KBC_HDD and HMD Humanitarian Response Plan, KBC will assist people in need in hard-to-reach and under-served areas in Kachin State, KBC will operate activities across three townships. This emergency response addresses to the suffering conflict affected 33,795 ( Men 9,492, Women 13,262, Boy 4,457, Girl 6,584 ), who are living at 19 IDPs relatives, 5 Returnees villages and 6 host communities in Waing Maw, Shwegu and Moehnyin (Northeast, Kachin ) . Planed emergency response will be worked for the 1st of September 2023 to 31st of August, 2024. In terms of constraint of accessibility in responses, this proposed project mainly focus on accessing to Health, Nutrition, Food Security and WASH inclusiveness of conflict affected IDPs relatives, Returnees villages and host communities of Northeast, Kachin to saving lives.ltbrgtAs the above mention, in this project, four sectors will be delivered to those who are in needs. As the first sector food security mainly aims to provide basic food assistance for life-saving to the conflict-affected Internal Displaced people from 4 camps for 4140 affected IDPs in Northeast, Kachin through cash transfer modality with “cash in envelop”, to meet their basis food needs with a period of 4 month (covering October 2023 to January 2024). For the next is WASH intervention will be implemented 9 IDPs sites( KCA 4 camps and SAC 5 camps) in Waingmaw township (Northeast, Kachin ) where the needs of the people are critical. The activities of WASH will promote safety and sufficient and to improve sanitation facilities. In addition, the WASH infrastructure, the hygiene promotion and behavior change activities will be conducted in the targeted camps. So, these two sector will be run by HDD. ltbrgtThe third is the nutrition services will cover 13 target areas with a population of - 11,988 ( Men 3,880, Women 5,220, Boy1,435, Girls 1453) in Waingmaw Township where political instability is present and displacement is active and dynamic. The activities will include both Nutrition specific and sensitive services with regular coordination and technical guidance from Nutrition Cluster, UNICEF. The forth one is health which is essential and will be provided to 26 target areas in Waingmaw, Shwegu and Moehnyin townships where the health needs and gaps are present. This project will cover 32,964 ( Men 9,185, Women 12,821, Boy 4,421, Girl 6,537), . For the most effective and realistic services for the community, guidance is regularly sought from Health Cluster, WHO which includes all possible services such as mobile services, community based fixed clinic services, patient referral support and awareness raising activities. HMD will implement these two sectors.lt/pgt
